name: Sports-betting risk & odds management
topic: Beava's current market position — competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Generic real-time substrate at virtually every operator: Redis (counters, sliding windows, RedisBloom/CMS/Top-K modules) and Aerospike (DraftKings' public reference architecture — clusters expanding from 6–10 to 16–20 nodes at Super Bowl peak, per-replica memory 3–5 GB → 25 GB, TTLs from minutes to a day). Apache Kafka + Apache Flink is the canonical streaming backbone — FanDuel publicly uses Confluent + Flink, Ververica/Decodable explicitly market sports betting as a Flink reference vertical, and Flink 2.0 (Mar 2025) is positioned for this workload. bet365 uses Push Technology's Diffusion for client-fanout in-play. Hazelcast for in-memory grid. ClickHouse/Pinot/Druid power trader dashboards. Tinybird is a published FanDuel real-time API vendor. PostgreSQL/Oracle/NewSQL hold the wager system-of-record. Managed feature stores (Tecton, Hopsworks, Feast, Chalk) are conspicuously rare in sportsbook trading because the sub-50 ms bet-acceptance budget is below typical ML-inference feature-store SLAs — they show up in offline modelling and stake-factoring score serving but not in the bet-acceptance hot path.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Three tiers of named incumbents. (1) B2B turnkey sportsbook + trading platforms (most direct competitive context for beava as a substrate): Kambi (Turnkey + Tzeract AI trading; Q1 2025 revenue EUR 43.5M +4.8% YoY, 10.2% operator trading margin, AI pricing/trading now drives >1/3 of operator GGR across the network; Penn Entertainment retail-only Kambi extension to July 2027 after Penn moved online to in-house post-ESPN), Sportradar (2025 revenue EUR 1.29B / +17% YoY; Managed Trading Services turnover USD 52B / +26% YoY at ~11% client margin; UFDS AI flagged 1,116 suspicious matches across 84 countries in 2025; FIFA integrity partnership renewed Mar 2026 through 2031), Genius Sports (2024 revenue ~USD 511M; BetVision computer-vision in-play deployed to Hard Rock Bet over 23k games in 2025, expanded to soccer May 2025 and tennis Jan 2026), OddsMatrix/EveryMatrix (2023 OddsMatrix profitability EUR 191M; 40+ sportsbook customers), OpticOdds (Copilot sportsbook management, 200+ sportsbook feeds), GR8 Tech, Altenar, BtoBet/NeoGames, Digitain, FSB, BetConstruct, Pronet, GAN. (2) Micro-betting + ML pricing: Simplebet (acquired by DraftKings 2024 for ~USD 200M), Huddle, Metric Gaming, Quants AI. (3) Integrity / RG / AML specialists: Sportradar Integrity Services + UFDS, US Integrity, IBIA Integrity Exchange, ESIC (esports); Mindway AI BetBuddy, Bettor Sense, Optimove for RG; GeoComply (geo), Sumsub/Jumio (KYC), ComplyAdvantage and Featurespace ARIC (now Visa, acquired ~USD 937M Apr 2025) for AML. Recent shakeout: Bayes Esports filed for insolvency Sep 2025 and IP was acquired by GRID; Tipico exited US in 2024 (sold to LeoVegas/MGM); Betfred ended US online Jul 2025; Caesars CEO Tom Reeg has paused the digital spinoff after Q2 2025 net loss USD 82M; bet365 NJ market share is growing (+51% YoY Jan 2026, ~USD 7M revenue in Mar 2026, mid-tier) but no monopoly — NJ has 12 active books and FanDuel+DraftKings still ~62% of revenue.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Proprietary-dominated. Kambi, Sportradar, Genius Sports, OddsMatrix, OpticOdds, Simplebet, Huddle, Bayes/GRID, Featurespace/ARIC, Mindway, BetBuddy are all closed-source commercial platforms. Generic substrate is mixed: Redis added AGPLv3 May 2025 alongside RSALv2/SSPLv1 (still a procurement headache for some operators), Valkey is BSD-3 under the Linux Foundation and is the cloud-default (Ubuntu 26.04 ships Valkey as the redis package), Aerospike is proprietary with a community-edition carve-out, Flink/Kafka are Apache-2.0. Beava's Apache-2.0 status is a genuine wedge versus the proprietary B2B trading platforms and a tie versus Flink/Kafka/Valkey for the DIY stack.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium. There is no single hyperscaler SKU labelled 'sportsbook risk engine', so the threat is indirect: Confluent Cloud + Flink (now Spark Real-Time Mode in Databricks competes for the same niche), AWS MSK + Managed Flink + ElastiCache (Valkey) + DynamoDB, Google Cloud Pub/Sub + Dataflow + Memorystore, and Azure Event Hubs + Stream Analytics + Cache for Redis all together can synthesize a 'good enough' alternative for tier-2/3 operators and B2B vendors. Databricks 2024 acquisition of Tecton's online-store assets and the 2025 push of Real-Time Mode in Spark mean the hyperscaler bundle is improving fast. The structural mitigant for beava: tier-1 US operators are forced into per-state, per-jurisdiction stacks (FanDuel uses AWS Local Zones / Wavelength / Outposts) which favours single-binary deployable units over managed multi-region SaaS — the very topology beava is shaped for.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Producers expected by buyers: wager-acceptance microservices (HTTP/JSON or in-house TCP push from the wager gateway), odds engine (price_update events from the trading platform — Kambi, Genius, Sportradar, in-house), score feed (Sportradar UOF, Genius LiveData, OPTA, IMG Arena, Stats Perform — typically Kafka or AMQP bridge; TxODDS Fusion advertises 8–10 ms odds), payment processor deposit/withdrawal, GeoComply geo-check webhooks, Sumsub/Jumio KYC, responsible-gambling intervention service. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits in-house microservices and webhook producers; framed-TCP+msgpack :8081 fits high-throughput odds-feed gateways and wager-acceptance services with sub-ms feature reads. The friction: buyers expect a Kafka-first ingestion model — beava's push-on-event design is materially fresher (no broker hop) than Kafka→Flink→Redis, but the procurement question 'how does beava plug into our existing Kafka topics?' must be answered with a documented adapter pattern, otherwise it is rejected as 'doesn't fit our stack' rather than evaluated on merit.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Deterministic rules engine (liability_cap, max-stake-per-market, state-mandated RG deposit limits, AML CTR/SAR > USD 10k, geo-fence, self-exclude — must be exact, auditable, regulator-defensible) is paired with ML scorers (XGBoost/LightGBM stake-factoring, Bayesian sharp-detection ensembles, RG ML scorers like Bettor Sense / Mindway BetBuddy, anomaly transformers). Beava as a pure feature backend sits before both, with the same batch_get path feeding rules and models — its natural seam.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: 1) Single binary that fits the per-state / per-jurisdiction regulated topology US sportsbooks are forced into (FanDuel AWS Local Zones/Wavelength/Outposts; Aerospike per-region clusters at DraftKings) — no Kafka cluster, no Flink job manager, no Redis Sentinel, just a Rust binary next to the wager-acceptance service. 2) ~60 aggregation primitives natively cover the velocity / liability / distribution / distance shapes sportsbook risk lives on, including a distance primitive that directly expresses CLV (price-taken vs closing-price distribution distance) and impossible-travel for VPN / multi-account — without writing Flink SQL, Redis Lua, or hand-rolled Aerospike UDFs. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits the bet-acceptance latency budget (well inside the DraftKings/Aerospike-class envelope, beats Kafka→Flink→materialized-view pipelines by a fair margin). 4) Apache-2.0 with no open-core rug — attractive to mid-tier operators (Hard Rock Bet, Fanatics, Rush Street, PointsBet, Underdog, PrizePicks, Sleeper, every state-lottery sportsbook) and especially to B2B vendors (Altenar, BtoBet, GR8 Tech, FSB, Digitain) who cannot or will not depend on Redis Source Available drift or a managed-cloud feature store. 5) Native composite-key aggregations — (event_id, market_id, selection_id), (account_id, sport, market_type), (market_id, time_bucket), (device_fp, ip_hash) are first-class in @bv.table; Redis requires hand-rolled hash-of-hash schemes and Aerospike requires UDF work. 6) Deterministic, explainable primitives — auditor / SEC-disclosure / SOC1 / state-regulator-friendly compared to Flink SQL pipelines whose recovery semantics auditors struggle to certify (DraftKings, Flutter, Entain, Penn, Caesars all SEC-registered). 7) Refuse-on-network-FS bias maps directly to the local-NVMe-WAL pattern DraftKings-class operators already deploy.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Severe and well-defined, roughly in priority order: 1) No TLS / no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for any production deployment in a state-licensed, SOC2, PCI-DSS or GDPR-exposed sportsbook; effectively limits beava to in-VPC / mTLS-proxy deployments. This is the single largest blocker for the domain. 2) No triggers / 'fire callback when (event_id, market_id, selection_id).net_position crosses liability_cap, suspend market' / 'when (account_id).clv_streak > N, drop stake_factor bracket' — sportsbook risk is fundamentally event-driven (suspend, reprice, hedge, stake-factor, RG-intervene, AML-flag) and polling 30+ features per wager wastes round-trips on the bet-acceptance hot path; this is the single most-cited workflow gap. 3) No in-process sharding — tier-1 US operators (DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM) at Super Bowl/March Madness scale exceed single-node beava (FanDuel handled 16.6M bets on Super Bowl Sunday 2025), and B2B platforms (Kambi, Sportradar MTS) need horizontal partition by tenant. 4) In-memory only, no audit-grade 5–7 year archive — AML / SAR / integrity-monitoring records require regulator-grade retention (UK GC LCCP 5+ years, William Hill cites 7 years, FinCEN BSA, FATF gambling guidance 2024); beava must document the WAL→Parquet/Iceberg/Snowflake archive integration. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives (per-tenant namespaces/quotas/audit) — Kambi, OddsMatrix, OpticOdds, Altenar, GR8 Tech B2B substrates need this. 6) No secondary indexes / no 'top-K (event, market) by liability_z over last 1 h' — kills the trader-dashboard surface (Kambi, OddsMatrix advertise this exact view). 7) Strict-exact monetary accumulation needs an explicit benchmark and bet_id idempotency proof under crash+replay — money is on the line. 8) No native correlation engine for SGP / parlay leg correlation (OpticOdds SGP Engine, FanDuel correlation models). 9) No published integration with Sportradar UOF, Genius LiveData, OPTA, IMG Arena, TxODDS Fusion odds feeds — all proprietary binary/AMQP. 10) No native graph / cohort primitives for collusion / bonus-abuse / coordinated-sharp ring detection (Sportradar UFDS territory). 11) No PII-at-rest hashing, no per-namespace retention, no GDPR Art. 17 right-to-erasure cascading. 12) No public sportsbook demo / case study / vertical example in the repo.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: No public beava users in this segment. [uncertain] No GitHub issues, Discord threads, or conference talks reference beava in a sports-betting context. The repo ships demos for adtech, ecommerce, and fraud — no sportsbook vertical. Comparable production systems that legitimise the shape are well-documented: DraftKings/Aerospike (public case study — 6–10 to 16–20 node Kubernetes cluster, 25 GB per-replica peak), FanDuel (Tinybird real-time API, Snowplow Super Bowl personalisation, Optimove martech, Confluent+Flink, AWS Local Zones), Kambi (Q1 2025 EUR 43.5M revenue, 10.2% operator trading margin, AI pricing/trading >1/3 of operator GGR, Bragg/711 Belgian launch May 2026), Sportradar (2025 revenue EUR 1.29B / MTS USD 52B turnover / UFDS 1,116 flagged matches across 84 countries / FIFA renewal through 2031), Genius Sports BetVision (Hard Rock Bet 23k+ games, soccer May 2025, tennis Jan 2026), OddsMatrix (40+ sportsbooks, 1.5M bets/day, EUR 191M 2023 profitability), bet365 NJ (+51% YoY Jan 2026), Ververica/Confluent sports-betting reference materials, RisingWave sports-betting use-case page, Databricks Data+AI Summit 2025 sports-modelling sessions. Beava knows who the buyer is (Trading Director / Head of Risk / Head of Integrity / Head of RG / Head of AML), but has zero proof points in the segment today.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Watch — adversarial-grade fit on the technical shape (composite-key velocity, sub-ms reads, single-binary regional topology, Apache-2.0 vs proprietary B2B incumbents) but the disqualifier stack (no TLS/auth, no triggers, no sharding, no audit archive, no multi-tenancy) is large and the procurement cycle at regulated operators is 6–18 months. Best 12-month posture is a sportsbook demo + B2B-platform conversation (Altenar, BtoBet, GR8 Tech, FSB) rather than a tier-1 operator pursuit.
